transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brought me in is that I just don't feel like myself anymore. I barely talk to anyone these days. I just sort of... go flat and quiet. Even at work, getting started on my cleaning route feels like I'm trying to push a loaded cart uphill. I just don't have it in me.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, it's been building up for a while now. I'd say... about a year and five months. It really started ever since I had to leave my old apartment and move out of my old neighborhood.
Have you heard voices when no one else was present?

Yeah, I have. Um... it mostly happens when I’m mopping after hours at work. I'll hear a man’s voice say my name, or... or tell me I’ve missed a spot. It sounds clear as day, just like he’s standing right by the stairwell. But when I look over, there's nobody there.
Have you heard this voice during times when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah, I have. Um... there was a stretch of several weeks a little while back where my mood had actually lifted some. I was getting through my meals and my work shifts a little better, not feeling quite so heavy. But even then, I still heard my name being called in the stairwell. And... well, I also stayed convinced that the hallway cameras were being used to track me, even when I wasn't feeling so down.
Since these problems began, have you felt significantly depressed for most of the time?

Yeah, I have. Really, for most of the time since the move, the sadness and the low energy... and just this feeling of guilt and not having any interest in things, it's all just been there in the background. Even on the days when the voices or my worries about the cameras are the main thing on my mind, that heavy, depressed feeling is still sitting right there underneath it all.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you heard the voice or believed the cameras were tracking you while feeling completely free of depressive symptoms?

Yeah, like I mentioned a minute ago, there was that stretch of several weeks. My mood had lifted, and I wasn't feeling depressed at all during that time. I was getting through my meals and my work shifts fine. But even though the sadness was gone for those couple of weeks, I still heard my name being called in the stairwell, and I was still completely convinced those hallway cameras were tracking me.
